assessment.summary: JAK2 is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 171 PDB structures (best resolution 1.3Å), over 19,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 12 approved drugs including ruxolitinib, baricitinib, and fedratinib. The target has extensive structural, chemical, and clinical validation across multiple disease indications including myeloproliferative neoplasms and inflammatory conditions. Druggability is unambiguously high with a deep and well-characterized chemical space.
evidence_gaps: Selectivity over closely related JAK family members (JAK1, JAK3, TYK2) remains a challenge for next-generation inhibitors, and isoform-selective chemical probes are still being developed
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP-competitive kinase domain are less well-characterized structurally
Resistance mechanisms to approved JAK2 inhibitors (e.g., in myelofibrosis) are not fully elucidated at the structural level
PROTAC/degrader approaches targeting JAK2 are emerging but clinical validation is limited
Covalent inhibitor strategies for JAK2 are underexplored relative to the ATP-competitive space
